facts: BasePyTreeCheckpointHandler.save blocks until copy and commit complete.
B2 BlockingHandler therefore serializes large PyTree item saves at item-completion granularity.
Orbax async_serialize_from_host awaits TensorStore fragment writes and uses can_reference_source_data_indefinitely=True.
Default OCDBT TensorStore context cache_pool#ocdbt.total_bytes_limit is 100000000 bytes, so the configured OCDBT cache pool alone cannot explain tens of GiB growth.

residue_evidence.interpretation: The residue is consistent with params completing first and train_state being partially written second under the intended serial-item contract.

resource_reconstruction.interpretation: The observed resident step0 state plus already-written OCDBT bytes plus the prospectively bounded D2H staging budget account for about 93.2% of the 52GiB ceiling before Python/JAX/TensorStore and other runtime overhead. This strongly motivates a write/cache-lifetime mechanism review but does not prove kill-time file-cache residency because historical cgroup memory.stat was not captured.

negative_diagnostic.test: 64MB CPU local TensorStore write weakref/RSS smoke comparing can_reference_source_data_indefinitely=true versus false
negative_diagnostic.interpretation: The hard-coded TensorStore reference flag is not by itself sufficient to explain B2 host-memory accumulation; a simple local write released the source array after await.

missing_evidence: kill-time cgroup memory.stat anon/file/file_dirty/file_writeback breakdown was not retained
non-root kernel logs do not expose a more detailed OOM memory breakdown
there is no authorization to replay B2 merely to collect diagnostics
